findings.title: Generated update rule omits required 2026-03-10 API parameters
findings.evidence: The generated rule is exactly {"type":"update"}; GitHub documents parameters.update_allows_fetch_and_merge as required for an update rule.
findings.impact: The proposed non-dev confinement POST is not a valid exact operation under the pinned API and can fail with REST validation error.
findings.required_change: Emit and test the complete update-rule parameters after choosing the intended fetch-and-merge behavior, and validate operation bodies against the pinned API schema.

findings.title: Owner and broker may resolve to the same bypass actor
findings.evidence: A deterministic same-user-id owner/broker probe returned ready_for_review with two ruleset POSTs while the always-bypass actor id equaled the broker user id.
findings.impact: The admitted broker can bypass the update rule, defeating the claimed non-dev update restriction even when its token has administration:none.
findings.required_change: Reject owner/broker identity aliasing by immutable user id, check login consistency, and add same-id adversarial tests.

findings.title: Reviewed workflow source is not bound to the accepted required check
findings.evidence: The ruleset binds only context and integration_id, while the runtime accepts any syntactically valid workflow path and drops that path from the normalized check. GitHub states required status checks do not account for workflow or event trigger type.
findings.impact: Another workflow under the same app with the same job/check name can satisfy the destination and local predicates without being the reviewed workflow path/source.
findings.required_change: Bind the actual run path/source through policy, plan, observation, and decision, or qualify GitHub's workflow ruleset primitive; test same-app same-name workflow collisions.

findings.title: Canonical observation does not contain the effective policy state it labels complete
findings.evidence: The observation has completeness booleans but no immutable repository id, effective-rule bodies, or classic branch-protection record. The refresh narrative's repository id and dev protection 404 are absent from the digested observation.
findings.impact: Same-name repository replacement or classic-protection drift can leave observation_digest and plan_digest unchanged even though GitHub aggregates branch protection with rulesets.
findings.required_change: Digest immutable repository identity and bounded effective policy records, including classic protection or verified absence; do not let an unaccompanied true visibility flag unlock operations.
